references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 19:13-15|Matthew 19:13-15] tells the same event where people brought children to Jesus so that he would lay his hands on them and pray, but the disciples rebuked them. Jesus answered: "Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."

The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 10:13-16|Mark 10:13-16] gives the most detailed account of this event, where Jesus is indignant with the disciples and says that the kingdom of God belongs to children, and that whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.

The immediate continuation in [ref:Luk 18:16-17|Luke 18:16-17] shows Jesus' response: He called the children to him and said that the kingdom of God belongs to such as these, and emphasized that one must receive the kingdom of God like a little child.

In [ref:Matt 18:1-4|Matthew 18:1-4], Jesus uses a little child as an example and says that whoever humbles themselves like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. This underscores the same attitude toward children as in Luke 18:15.

In [ref:1 Mos 48:13-14|Gen 48:13-14], Joseph brings his sons to Jacob so that he may bless them by laying hands on them. This is an Old Testament parallel to bringing children to a spiritual leader for blessing.

In [ref:Luk 9:47-48|Luke 9:47-48], Jesus takes a little child and sets him beside himself, saying that whoever receives this child in his name receives him. The disciples' rejection of the children in 18:15 stands in contrast to Jesus' own attitude toward children.

In [ref:Luk 9:49-50|Luke 9:49-50], Jesus rebukes the disciples for preventing someone from acting in his name. The same pattern is seen in 18:15, where the disciples again try to prevent people from coming to Jesus, and Jesus corrects them.
